Privacy notice

Draft — pending review by counsel. This notice describes what the current code does; it has not yet been reviewed by a lawyer. The name of the operator and a contact address are still to be added.

Draft dated November 13, 2026.

In short

  • The map, forecasts and downloads work without an account.
  • If you make an account, we store what you save in it. You can export or delete all of it yourself, at any time.
  • We run no advertising and no third-party tracking scripts.
  • We do not sell your information.

Your account

You sign in with a passkey. There is no password, and we do not ask for or store an email address, phone number or real name. You may give the account a display name (up to 60 characters); that is optional. We store your passkey’s public key and the dates it was used, never the private key, which stays on your device. An account can hold up to 10 passkeys.

When you sign in we keep a record of that sign-in, with the first 80 characters of your browser’s description (for example “Chrome on Mac”), so the account panel can show where you are signed in and let you sign out other devices. We set one cookie, __Host-sc_session, when you sign in. It keeps you signed in for 30 days from your last use and is not used for tracking.

What an account stores, and for how long

What we store Why How long
Account id, optional display name, passkeys To sign you in. Until you delete your account. There is no automatic deletion of unused accounts.
Sign-in sessions To keep you signed in and list your devices. Until they expire (30 days after last use) or you sign out.
Saved trips: area, forecast point, species, date, hours, wind, gust and sea limits, optional boat details and plan To check the forecast for your trip and send alerts. Removed 90 days after the trip date, or when you delete the trip.
Alerts we sent you and delivery records To show alert history and avoid sending twice. 90 days.
Notification devices: your browser’s push address and its encryption keys (up to 5) To deliver alerts. Until you turn notifications off, the push service reports the device gone, or you delete your account.
Comfort ratings: area, time, a 1–10 rating and the conditions you entered To tune comfort estimates. 365 days.
Private catch log: time, method, species, outcome, count, optional position and note Your own record. Until you delete the entry or your account. There is no automatic deletion.
Saved spots: name, position and optional note (up to 100) Your own private places. Until you delete the spot or your account. There is no automatic deletion.
Request counters: a one-way hash and a count To limit how fast requests can be made. About two minutes (about two days for the daily boat-lookup counter).

Your catch log and saved spots are private to your account. No public page, feed or other account reads them. Expired records are removed by a scheduled cleanup, so removal can lag the dates above by a short time. Deleted records may remain for a time in backups kept by our hosting provider.

Your position

In the account panel, “Use my position” asks your browser for one fresh location only when you press it. It fills the position boxes. Nothing is sent to SkipperCast until you press Save. A catch-log position is optional; a saved spot needs one. Elsewhere on the site, such as finding a nearby port or the boat-position tool, your location is used in the browser only and is not sent to SkipperCast.

Export and delete

In the trip-alerts panel, “Export my records” downloads one JSON file with your account details, trips, comfort ratings, alerts, devices (the push service name and date only), catch log and saved spots. “Delete account” (account panel) or “Delete all my records” (trip-alerts panel) removes all of that at once, including your passkeys and sessions. It cannot be undone and there is no waiting period. To correct a record, change it and save it again.

AI boat lookup

The boat lookup may not be available. When it is, and you press “look up” on your boat profile, the boat description you typed (3 to 120 characters, for example “Parker 2320 SL 2019”) is sent to Anthropic, which runs a Claude model with web search to find the builder’s specifications. Your account id is not sent. Only signed-in people can use it, 20 times a day. We keep the answer in a shared cache for up to 30 days, keyed by the text, so the same lookup is not repeated for anyone; do not type personal information into that box. How Anthropic handles what it receives is set by Anthropic’s own terms.

Usage statistics

Our pages are built to send a small set of anonymous counts to our own Cloudflare analytics dataset, not to an analytics company. At the time of this draft the server discards them and stores none; if storing is switched on, this notice is updated first. What the counts are:

  • Visit steps, once per page load and region, with the region, the site build and, where the link had one, whether the visit came from a text, Instagram, Facebook or our printed QR code. The map sends map_viewed, port_selected, spot_saved and offline_saved. The home page sends error reports only.
  • Error reports when a page hits an uncaught error: the message with web-address queries, positions, emails and long numbers removed and cut short, the script’s file name only, and the site build.
  • Server counts: each request to our server is counted by page type, method, status and speed, without your IP address, account or what you typed.

There is no cookie, no storage and no visitor, session or device id in these counts. If your browser sends Do Not Track or Global Privacy Control, the pages send neither visit steps nor error reports. Cloudflare keeps such counts for three months by default; we set no other period.

On your device

Your home port, boat profile, comfort limits, language, map choices, a private map log (up to 500 entries, including positions you pick on the map) and saved offline map data are kept in your browser’s storage and never sent to us. Clearing your browser’s site data removes them.

Other companies that see your visit

Our site runs on Cloudflare, which handles your IP address and requests to deliver and secure it and keeps standard request logs; a request for a forecast carries its latitude and longitude. Your browser loads map tiles and public data directly from OpenStreetMap, NOAA (weather, tides, charts, cloud imagery), the National Weather Service, the California Department of Fish and Wildlife (protected-area boundaries, through ArcGIS), the U.S. Geological Survey (aerial imagery) and GitHub (backup copies of data files). Each sees your IP address under its own policy. Alerts are delivered through your browser’s push service (Google, Mozilla, Apple or Microsoft).

Changes and contact

We will change the date at the top of this page when the notice changes. The operator’s name and a contact address will be added here before launch.
